record.title: Beijing solicits AI cyber-defense research and adversarial test-platform proposals
record.summary: Beijing’s science and technology commission opened a 2026 call for AI-enabled cybersecurity-defense research proposals. It has two tracks: enterprise-led AI defense products and a high-fidelity adversarial test platform led by universities or research institutes. The company track requires at least 2:1 matching funds and limits projects to one year; applications close Oct 29, 2026 at 18:00. The notice reports no award amounts, selected teams, research outputs or measured defenses.
organizations: Beijing Municipal Science and Technology Commission

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: On Oct 20, the Beijing Municipal Science and Technology Commission and Zhongguancun Administrative Committee opened a 2026 solicitation for reserve research projects in AI-enabled cybersecurity defense, with online applications due Oct 29, 2026 at 18:00.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The notice defines two tracks: enterprise-led development of AI cyber-defense technologies/products, and a university/research-institute high-fidelity adversarial testing platform with automated testing capability and high-quality attack-defense datasets. The company track requires enterprise matching funds at a ratio of at least 2:1 to the science funding and caps project duration at one year.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_LIMITATION
claims.text: The notice establishes a proposal call and target scope only. It gives no award amount, selected projects, completed research, technical performance or deployment outcome.

evidence_gaps.description: No award amount, selected projects, award recipients or funded work plan is included in the solicitation.
No technical artifact, evaluation protocol, attack-defense dataset, benchmark result or deployment evidence is reported because this is a proposal-stage call.

brief.importance_rationale: If funded and completed, the paired call could direct short-cycle public R&D toward both AI-based cyber-defense products and high-fidelity adversarial testing of their limits. The announced scope is specific and relevant, but award size, selected projects and technical outcomes are unknown.
limitations: This is an official solicitation, not evidence of selected or funded projects.
The call provides no total funding amount, per-project award range, beneficiary list or outcome data.
Its technical objectives and intended demonstrations are stated goals; no defensive efficacy or testing-platform validity is shown.
organizations: Beijing Municipal Science and Technology Commission

technical.claimed_result: No research outcome is claimed; the notice states intended project objectives and application requirements.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official notice establishes two proposal tracks, applicant constraints, matching requirement, one-year duration cap and deadline. It does not establish funding awards, project delivery or defensive efficacy.
technical.mechanism: The call proposes a product track for AI detection, attack-chain analysis and defense, alongside a high-fidelity automated adversarial test platform and attack-defense datasets to assess and improve products.

technical.strongest_baseline: Not applicable: this is a proposal solicitation and reports no completed project or baseline measurement.

brief.why_it_matters: The paired tracks connect AI-defense product development with adversarial evaluation of those products, including automated testing and high-quality attack-defense datasets. If funded and completed, this could influence regional cyber-AI research and validation capacity. The solicitation alone shows neither the funding committed nor any technical result.
